label: duplicate-test-coverage
name: Two tests on one call, an arithmetic-only case subsumed by the outcome case, or a new test binary for a path an existing binary already executes
description: What breaks: coverage that protects no distinct behavior. A GENERATE arm and a new section both run the same four copy_token parities through book::append (4188336316, check 4 as written); the pool_worker arithmetic case duplicates the outcome case that REQUIREs the same mapping (4146998951 'it could be dropped'); a whole new unit-test binary with its own add_catch_test and cost row when t_llama_unit already constructs and destroys KV books (3970127694 'Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test?'). Procedure (check 4 widened): also fire on a new test translation unit whose exercised production function an existing test binary already calls; propose moving the check and its define to that target.
disposition_reason: Check 4 compares two units in one PR; the corpus adds placement of a new test binary against an existing one that already executes the path.
agent_feasibility: yes: pairwise call/branch comparison of new units; for new test targets, grep existing test binaries for calls into the function under test.

members.concern: A new GENERATE in the poison section and the new 'token copies keep bits in all four parity combinations' section both drive all four copy_token parities through book::append; the bit-exact section covers more and one parity already protects the NaN-zeroing rule, so one of the two is duplicate coverage.

detection.trigger: The PR adds or widens two test units (a GENERATE arm added to an existing SECTION plus a new SECTION) that make the same production call (book::append -> copy_token) with the same token sets and source type.
detection.procedure: name the production call of each unit and follow it to the leaf function with branches the diff changed (copy_token even/odd parity branches in v_vnni.hpp); map each GENERATE value and token index to the branch it reaches; simulate write order so a slot counts as observed only if not overwritten before the assertion reads it; compare the (branch, slot, reference) sets of the two units pairwise.
detection.question: Is there a deliberate code break that fails unit A but passes unit B? If none, A is duplicate coverage; if some, give B that observation and drop A.

members.quote: This `GENERATE` and the new "token copies keep bits in all four parity combinations" section (line 3664) both run all four `copy_token` parities through `book::append`; the bit-exact one covers more. One parity here already protects the NaN zeroing, so one of these is duplicate coverage.
members.note: Anchored at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3298 (96a6220ab6): `GENERATE(EVEN_START_DST_TOKENS_2, ODD_START_DST_TOKENS_3)`. references/pr4557-misses.md (W5) finds the point only partly right: the two GENERATE values reach two different partner-clearing branches of copy_token (andnot at v_vnni.hpp:359-364 vs srli at :378-384), and the bit-exact section fills the whole page so its last copies overwrite every odd partner before the comparison reads them, i.e. it cannot observe partner clearing. The author nevertheless removed the GENERATE (back to dst_tokens 3).

members.concern: Nit: the test case that checks the pool_worker arithmetic duplicates the next case (rows keyed by pool worker), which already asserts the same mapping values and additionally the outcome that matters (counts land in the rows of the threads that ran the work, main-helper row stays zero); the arithmetic-only case can be dropped.

detection.trigger: The diff adds two TEST_CASEs (or sections) that call the same new helper with the same named constants, where one case only asserts the helper's return values and the other asserts those same values (REQUIRE on the helper result) on its way to checking a downstream effect.
detection.procedure: For each new test unit, list the production calls and the constants fed to them. Find pairs where unit A's assertion set is a subset of what unit B asserts or implies (B calls the same helper with the same inputs and REQUIREs the same results before using them). Name what B checks beyond A. If A adds nothing, propose dropping A and state what B keeps.
detection.question: Is there a code break that fails the arithmetic-only case but passes the outcome case that REQUIREs the same mapping?

members.quote: This one adds only the arithmetic of a one-line function, so it could be dropped.
members.note: Verified at 0f784c44ff t/t_attn_stats.cpp:640-657 ('attn-stats pool_worker: the last n_attn_workers pool workers run attention', CHECKs on pool_worker(WORKER_0, SPLIT_1) == WORKER_2 etc.) and :659+ ('rows keyed by pool worker', REQUIRE(row == WORKER_2) / REQUIRE(row == WORKER_1) then add_visits/note_attn_job and row checks). The first case also checks the off state answers the same, which the second does not; Wade still judged it droppable. Check 4 as written requires the same GENERATE/token set and leaf branches of a changed function; here the shared call is a branchless one-line helper, so the trigger text would not fire, the question does. Author dropped the case.

members.concern: Wade asks whether a whole new unit-test binary is needed for one regression test when t_llama_unit already constructs and destroys KV books (which executes log_kv_footprint), and proposes enabling _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS on that existing binary and adding the test there.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a new test translation unit and a new add_catch_test (or equivalent registration plus a config/test-benchmarks.json cost row) whose test exercises a production function that an existing test binary already calls.
detection.procedure: Take the function under test (log_kv_footprint, called from KV book constructors). grep t/ at BASE for tests that construct the same objects (t_llama_unit.cpp:1676 TEST_CASE 'book.append()' and the '[book append]' cases build and destroy books). Check whether the new binary's only distinguishing property is a per-target compile define (t/CMakeLists.txt:843-844 `DEFINES _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`) that could be applied to the existing target instead, and whether applying it there would break or slow its cases (the PR body later reports +2 % run time, 27/27 pass). AGENTS.md test policy: extend the closest existing test.
detection.question: Does an existing test binary already execute the code path under test, so that the new check belongs there (with its define moved to that target) instead of in a new binary with its own registration and cost row?

members.quote: Do we really need a whole new UT module for this test? `t_llama_unit` already has book.append() tests that construct and destroy KV books (which executes `log_kv_footprint`). Could we just enable _GLIBCSS_ASSERTIONS on that existing UT and incorporate this test there?
members.note: Anchored at line 1 of the new file t/t_kv_footprint_memorder.cpp at commit 7a7699b338 (a commit that adds the new binary's cost row to config/test-benchmarks.json; its message says 'The CI step bin/slice bench --check needs an entry for every registered test', so a new binary also costs a benchmark row). At that commit t/CMakeLists.txt:841-844 registered the new binary with DEFINES _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS and t_llama_unit.cpp:1676 had TEST_CASE 'book.append()' plus three '[book append]' cases. Wade misspells the macro as _GLIBCSS_ASSERTIONS. The author moved the test (final head: t/t_llama_unit.cpp +28, t/CMakeLists.txt +3, no new file) and Wade approved the next day. Relation to check 4: same theme (no duplicate test units; extend the closest existing test), but check 4's trigger needs two units making the same production call with the same inputs; here the concern is binary count and registration cost, not duplicate assertions, so the trigger as written does not fire. Memory file wade-move-test-question-pr4265.md records the word 'move' as his framing.

codex_bullets.bullet: Name the production behavior each assertion protects. A round trip, documented format, real regression, type boundary, or ownership invariant can justify exact values. Today's incidental rounding, structure, or helper arithmetic may not.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4557, 4596, asim 244). Claude checks 1 and 2 already encode this with procedures.

codex_bullets.bullet: Before calling tests duplicates, identify a plausible defect that one observes and the other misses. Include write order and overwritten observations. Consolidate only if the distinct protection survives and the result is clearer.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 4596, 4265). Claude check 4 already simulates write order and names the (branch, slot) pair.

codex_bullets.bullet: Prefer the closest existing test suite. A temporary workaround's regression test needs a documented reason and a replacement condition; do not remove protection before the underlying failure is understood.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4265, 4128, 2713, 2872). The workaround-needs-a-tracked-exit rule (2713, two comments) is new to the Claude skill.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (setup 2 quotes AGENTS.md "extend the closest existing test"; the workaround sentence has no check)
